subject.title: fix(ui): block agent-authored widget command prompts

question: Should agent-authored MCP App and widget text that begins with `/` or `!` remain categorically ineligible for host command interpretation, even after user confirmation?
rationale: The patch is mechanically small, but it deliberately narrows a user-visible capability at the trust boundary between sandboxed app content and authenticated host command handling; that policy choice should be explicitly owned by a maintainer.

options.title: Confirm the denial boundary
options.body: Approve the shared fail-closed rule and merge, keeping host commands available only through ordinary user-authored composer input.

options.title: Define an explicit app command capability
options.body: Pause this PR and design a separately authorized, typed app action instead of allowing command-shaped text through the conversational prompt route.

recommendation.title: Confirm the denial boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the shared fail-closed rule and merge, keeping host commands available only through ordinary user-authored composer input.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged MCP App bridge and are the most directly connected recent contributor to its prompt authority boundary.
